content.text:
The build is green. All tests pass.

## Summary

The registration date now always falls on a business day. I made the adjustment at the single point where the effective date is established, so every derived value stays consistent automatically.

**`BuildOwner.java`** — Computes the effective registration date (supplied in the request, or defaulted to `LocalDate.now()`), then rolls a Saturday forward two days / a Sunday forward one day to the next Monday before storing it on the owner. Because the membership number (`OwnerMapper.membershipNumber`, which reads `registrationDate.getYear()`) and all later steps read the date back off the owner, they now use the adjusted date with no further changes. This also changes the prior behaviour where a *supplied* weekend date was kept as-is.

**`RejectOverDailyLimit.java`** — The daily create-limit previously counted owners whose `registrationDate` equalled `LocalDate.now()`. It now counts owners sharing the new owner's *adjusted* registration date (`owner.getRegistrationDate()`), so the cap is enforced per adjusted business day — matching how stored owners' dates are now bucketed.

The acceptance test (`coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay`) asserts the defaulted `registrationDate` is never a weekend, and passes.
